name: Polignac
description: Polignac (also known as 'Jacks') is a classic French trick-avoidance game, a direct ancestor to modern games like Hearts. Played with a 32-card deck, the objective is to avoid capturing any Jacks, particularly the Jack of Spades, which is the 'Polignac'. It is a game of simplicity and social penalty, often played in French cafes as a quick gamble or a penalty game where the loser 'treats' the table.

Played with a 32-card deck, the objective is to avoid capturing any Jacks, particularly the Jack of Spades, which is the 'Polignac'. It is a game of simplicity and social penalty, often played in French cafes as a quick gamble or a penalty game where the loser 'treats' the table.

history.origins: Dates back to the early 19th century in France. It is named after the French Prime Minister Jules de Polignac, who was deeply unpopular at the timeâ€”hence why the most 'Penalty' card bears his name.
timeline: 1830: Named after the unpopular Polignac ministry.
1870s: Becomes a popular game in the French military (Zouaves).
1920s: Serves as the basis for the more complex game 'Barbu'.
Present: Still played in regional France, often as 'Le Valet Noir'.
history.cultural: In French culture, 'faire Polignac' means to accidentally catch the bad card, often resulting in good-natured mockery.
history.evolution: The game was simplified from earlier French games like 'L'Ambigu' to focus purely on the psychological tension of avoiding the 'Dirty Jack'.

setup.players: 4 is standard; 5 or 6 requires removing specific cards (like 7s) to make dealing even.

rules.objective: The aim of the game is to avoid capturing any Jacks in tricks, especially the Jack of Spades (Polignac). Penalty points are scored for each Jack taken; the first player to reach the agreed total loses the game.
rules.gameplay: Eldest hand leads first. Players must follow suit if possible; otherwise may play any card. The highest card of the suit led wins the trick. The winner of each trick leads to the next. There are no trumps. Players incur penalty points for capturing Jacks.
keyRules: Must follow suit when possible; otherwise any card may be played.
Highest card of the suit led wins the trick; winner leads next.
Jack of Spades (Polignac) costs 2 penalty points; each other Jack costs 1.

strategy.basic: Dump your Jacks! If you can't follow suit, play your Jacks immediately to ensure an opponent captures them. Save your lowest cards (7s and 8s) for the end of the round, as this is when the 'Big Jacks' usually come out as players run out of suit-fillers.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Polignac Trap': If you hold the Queen, King, or Ace of Spades, you are in danger of winning the Polignac. Try to lead Spades early in the round while everyone still has low Spades (7, 8, 9). This 'Clears' the suit and forces the person with the Jack to play it early when you aren't forced to win it.
strategy.advanced: The 'Capot' (Slam): In some house rules, if you capture ALL FOUR Jacks, you score zero points and everyone else gets 5. If you have a massive hand of high cards, you might intentionally 'Vacuum' up the Jacks to trigger this bonus. However, if you miss even one, you will have a disastrous score. It's the 'Shoot the Moon' of Polignac.
tips: Don't lead a suit you are 'Short' in (only 1 or 2 cards), as you want to keep that suit so you can 'Follow' safely later.
Watch the 'Polignac' card. Once it is played, the game becomes much safer for the high-card holders.

variations.name: Capot
variations.description: Before the opening lead, a player may bid capot: an undertaking to win every trick. If they succeed, each opponent loses 5 points; if they fail, the bidder loses 5.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Capot changes only scoring outcome; no engine constants or deal changes.

variations.name: General
variations.description: A player may announce before leading to the first trick that they will try to take all tricks. Success: all other players score 5 penalty points each. Failure: Jacks score 5 points in the usual way against the players who take them.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: General is a scoring variant only; no engine parameter overrides.

variations.name: Ace high variant
variations.description: If Ace is played as high (common in old French games), penalties attach to Queens instead of Jacks.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Ace-high shifts penalty cards to Queens; overrides not yet mapped.

scoring.description: Penalty points for capturing Jacks. Jack of Spades (Polignac) costs 2 points; each other Jack costs 1. First player to reach an agreed total (typically 10 or 20) loses the game.
scoring.winCondition: The first player to reach the agreed penalty total (e.g. 10 or 20 points) loses the game; lowest penalty total wins.
